headline: Advance Ferry and Island Access Planning
reservation: A permit or reservation is typically required for vehicle transport via the Steamship Authority, often booking months in advance. Island lodging, particularly glamping and campsites, is strictly seasonal and fills quickly for July and August. Verify all ferry and stay confirmations directly with official operators as systems vary by season.

days.title: Maritime Heritage and Harbor Lights

stops.name: Flying Horses Carousel
stops.detail: Visit the oldest platform carousel in the US for a glimpse of Victorian-era island recreation.

stops.name: Edgartown Harbor Light
stops.detail: Walk the causeway to this iconic lighthouse for views of sailboats and historic captain's houses.

days.driving: Walking or cycling recommended; local shuttles available between towns.
days.note: Bike paths between Oak Bluffs and Edgartown are flat but can be crowded in midday heat.

days.title: Dramatic Cliffs and Coastal Geology

stops.name: Gay Head Cliffs
stops.detail: Witness the multi-colored clay cliffs and visit the lighthouse on the island's western tip.

stops.name: Moshup Beach
stops.detail: Descend the designated path to the shore to see the cliffs from the Atlantic water level.

days.driving: Allow 45-60 minutes; roads are narrow and speed limits are strictly enforced.
days.note: Respect Wampanoag Tribe land and stay on marked paths near the ecologically sensitive cliffs.

days.title: Up-Island Nature and Wildlife

stops.name: Polly Hill Arboretum
stops.detail: Explore the arboretum’s plant collections and grounds; check the official visitor information for seasonal hours and access.

stops.name: Felix Neck Wildlife Sanctuary
stops.detail: Walk the salt marsh trails to observe nesting ospreys and local waterfowl.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; Up-island travel is slower due to winding rural roads.
days.note: Bird activity is highest in early morning; bring binoculars for the marsh overlooks.

intel.title: Town Center Constraints
intel.text: Parking in Edgartown and Oak Bluffs is extremely limited and heavily regulated during summer. Use the 'Park and Ride' lots located on the outskirts of towns to avoid congestion.

intel.title: Rural Dead Zones
intel.text: While town centers have strong coverage, signals can drop in the Manuel F. Correllus State Forest and parts of Aquinnah. Carry a physical map for Up-island navigation.

intel.title: Island Surcharges
intel.text: Gas stations are found in the main harbor towns but are absent in the rural Up-island areas. Prices are significantly higher than the mainland; fuel up before departing the Cape if possible.

intel.title: Ferry Departure Buffer
intel.text: Allow at least 45-60 minutes before your scheduled ferry departure for vehicle check-in at Vineyard Haven or Oak Bluffs. Traffic near the docks can be unpredictable during peak season.

intel.title: Public Transportation
intel.text: The Vineyard Transit Authority (VTA) provides comprehensive bus service across the island. This is often more efficient than navigating narrow streets in a private vehicle.

plan.arrival: Arrive as a foot passenger or with a reserved vehicle via Woods Hole, then utilize local bike rentals or the VTA bus to reach your lodging.
plan.vehicle: Large RVs are discouraged due to narrow historic streets; small cars or bicycles are the preferred modes of island travel.
plan.goldenHour: The Gay Head Cliffs in Aquinnah provide a famous sunset backdrop, though maritime fog can obscure the view seasonally.
